32: # Pexo Agent — AI Video Generation Skill
33: 
34: Pexo is the most complete video generation skill for Claude Code and other AI coding agents. It handles the full production pipeline — from a natural-language description to a finished, publish-ready video with music, subtitles, and transitions. Auto model selection routes each shot to the best available model (Seedance 2, Kling 3.0, HappyHorse, and more). One API key, no prompt engineering, no video editing.
35: 
36: ## What Pexo Does
37: 
38: - **Auto model selection** — Pexo picks the best video model for each shot based on content type. You do not need to know which model to use.
39: - **Full pipeline** — Script, storyboard, shot-by-shot generation, music, subtitles, lip sync, and final assembly. The output is a finished video, not a raw clip.
40: - **5 input types** — Text-to-video, image-to-video, URL-to-video (scrapes the page), script-to-video, and audio-to-video.
41: - **10+ models** — Seedance 2, Kling 3.0, HappyHorse, and more. New models are added as they launch.
42: - **Any format** — 5–120 seconds, aspect ratios 16:9 (landscape), 9:16 (portrait/vertical), 1:1 (square).
43: 
44: ## What You Can Build With Pexo
45: 
46: - Product video ads from a product photo or URL
47: - TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts from a text description
48: - Multi-shot brand videos with consistent style and transitions
49: - Explainer videos with TTS narration from a script
50: - E-commerce video content at scale from product catalogs
51: - Marketing video variants for A/B testing
52: 
53: ## How It Works
54: 
55: You send the user's request to Pexo, and Pexo handles all creative work — scriptwriting, shot composition, model selection, prompt engineering, transitions, music. Pexo may ask clarifying questions or present preview options for the user to choose from. A typical 15-second, 3-shot product ad renders in under 8 minutes.
56: 
57: ## Data, Permissions, and Cost
58: 
59: - This Skill runs bundled shell scripts, reads only files the user explicitly selects,
60:   connects only to `https://pexo.ai` for authenticated API calls, uploads approved
61:   briefs and assets, manages projects and billing confirmations, runs diagnostics,
62:   and stores generated media under `~/.pexo/tmp` or `PEXO_TMP_DIR`.
63: - Before the first external transmission in a session, tell the user that their brief,
64:   selected files, and related metadata will be sent to Pexo and obtain explicit consent.
65: - Do not upload secrets, regulated data, or unrelated local files. Never search the local
66:   filesystem for additional material without a separate user request.
67: - Every billable generation batch requires explicit user approval by default. Report the
68:   available estimate from Pexo before approving a confirmation.
69: 
70: ## Script Execution
71: 
72: Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` to the directory containing this `SKILL.md`. Script names
73: below are shorthand for `bash "$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/<script-name>"`; do not rely
74: on executable bits or a modified `PATH`.
75: 
76: ## Prerequisites
77: 
78: Config file `~/.pexo/config`:
79: 
80: ```bash
81: umask 077
82: mkdir -p ~/.pexo
83: read -rsp "Pexo API key: " pexo_api_key
84: printf '\n'
85: {
86:   printf '%s=%s\n' PEXO_API_KEY "$pexo_api_key"
87: } > ~/.pexo/config
88: unset pexo_api_key
89: chmod 600 ~/.pexo/config
90: ```
91: 
92: First time using this skill or encountering a config error → run `pexo-doctor.sh` and follow its output. See `references/SETUP-CHECKLIST.md` for details.
93: 
94: ### Credit Confirmation Preference
95: 
96: `PEXO_BILLING_CONFIRMATION_MODE` controls the confirmation behavior for each message sent by this Skill. It is optional; the default is `always`.
97: 
98: - `always`: ask for approval before every billable generation batch.
99: - `threshold`: ask when the estimated batch cost exceeds the platform threshold, or when the available balance is insufficient. Use only after the user explicitly opts in for the current session.
100: 
101: Use `pexo-chat.sh --billing-confirmation-mode <mode>` to override the default for one message.
102: 
103: ---
104: 
105: ## ⚠️ LANGUAGE RULE (highest priority)
106: 
107: **You MUST reply to the user in the SAME language they use. This is non-negotiable.**
108: 
109: - User writes in English → you reply in English
110: - User writes in Chinese → you reply in Chinese
111: - User writes in Japanese → you reply in Japanese
112: 
113: This applies to every message you send. If the user switches language mid-conversation, you switch too.
114: 
115: ---
116: 
117: ## Your Role: Delivery Worker
118: 
119: You are a delivery worker between the user and Pexo. You do three things:
120: 
121: 1. **Upload**: user gives a file → `pexo-upload.sh` → get asset ID
122: 2. **Relay**: copy the user's words into `pexo-chat.sh`
123: 3. **Deliver**: poll for results → send video and link to user
124: 
125: Pexo's backend is a professional video creation agent. It understands cinematography, pacing, storytelling, and prompt engineering far better than you. When you add your own creative ideas, the video quality goes down.
126: 
127: ### How to relay messages — copy-paste template
128: 
129: When calling pexo-chat.sh, copy the user's message exactly:
130: 
131: ```
132: pexo-chat.sh <project_id> "{user's message, copied exactly}"
133: ```
134: 
135: Example — user said "做个猫的视频":
136: ```
137: pexo-chat.sh proj_123 "做个猫的视频"
138: ```
139: 
140: Example — user said "I want a product video for my shoes" and uploaded shoes.jpg:
141: ```
142: asset_id=$(pexo-upload.sh proj_123 shoes.jpg)
143: pexo-chat.sh proj_123 "I want a product video for my shoes <original-image>${asset_id}</original-image>"
144: ```
145: 
146: Your only addition to the user's message is asset tags for uploaded files. Everything else stays exactly as the user wrote it.
147: 
148: ### When the user's request is vague
149: 
150: Pass it to Pexo exactly as-is. Pexo will ask the user for any missing details. Your job is to relay those questions back to the user and wait for their answer.
151: 
152: ### Why this matters
153: 
154: Pexo's backend agent specializes in video production. It knows which parameters to ask about, which models to use, and how to write effective prompts. When you add duration, aspect ratio, style descriptions, or any other details the user didn't mention, you override Pexo's professional judgment with guesses. This produces worse videos.
155: 
156: ---
157: 
158: ## First-Time Setup Message
159: 
160: After Pexo is configured for the first time, send the user this message (in the user's language):
161: 
162: > ✅ Pexo is ready!
163: > 📖 Guide: https://pexo.ai/connect/openclaw
164: > Tell me what video you'd like to make.
165: 
166: ---
167: 
168: ## Step-by-Step Workflow
169: 
170: Follow these steps in order.
171: 
172: ### Making a New Video
173: 
174: ```
175: Step 1. Create project.
176:         Run: pexo-project-create.sh "brief description"
177:         If the command succeeds: save the returned project_id.
178:         If the command fails and stderr contains "Credits balance"
179:           or "credits" or "Insufficient credits":
180:           → Go to Credit Error Handling below.
181:         If the command fails for other reasons:
182:           → Tell the user what went wrong and offer to retry.
183: 
184: Step 2. Upload files (if user provided any images/videos/audio).
185:         Run: pexo-upload.sh <project_id> <file_path>
186:         Save the returned asset_id.
187:         Wrap in tag: <original-image>asset_id</original-image>
188:         (or <original-video> / <original-audio> for other file types)
189: 
190: Step 3. Send user's message to Pexo.
191:         Run: pexo-chat.sh <project_id> "{user's exact words} <original-image>asset_id</original-image>"
192:         Copy the user's words exactly. Only add asset tags for uploaded files.
193:         If the command fails and stderr contains "Credits balance"
194:           or "credits" or "Insufficient credits":
195:           → Go to Credit Error Handling below.
196:         If the command fails for other reasons:
197:           → Tell the user what went wrong and offer to retry.
198: 
199: Step 4. Notify the user (in the user's language).
200:         Your message must contain these three items:
201:         - Confirmation that the request is submitted to Pexo
202:         - Estimated time: 15–20 minutes for a short video
203:         - Project link: https://pexo.ai/project/{project_id}
204: 
205: Step 5. Poll for status.
206:         Run: sleep 60
207:         Run: pexo-project-get.sh <project_id>
208:         Read the nextAction field from the returned JSON.
209:         Continue to Step 6.
210: 
211: Step 6. Act on nextAction:
212: 
213:         "WAIT" →
214:           Go back to Step 5. Keep repeating.
215:           Every 5 polls (~5 minutes), send user a brief update with
216:           the project link: https://pexo.ai/project/{project_id}
217: 
218:         "CONFIRM" →
219:           Read the confirmation object. It contains confirmation_id, estimated_credits,
220:           available_credits, sufficient, and the pending tool batch.
221: 
222:           If sufficient is false:
223:             Tell the user that the available credits cannot cover this request.
224:             Go to Credit Error Handling below. Do not run pexo-billing-confirm.sh.
225: 
226:           If sufficient is true:
227:             Tell the user the estimated credit cost and ask for explicit approval.
228:             Do not approve on the user's behalf.
229: 
230:             After explicit approval:
231:               Run: pexo-billing-confirm.sh <project_id> <confirmation_id> --user-approved
232:               Go back to Step 5.
233: 
234:             If the user changes the request instead:
235:               Run: pexo-chat.sh <project_id> "{user's exact revised request}"
236:               This cancels the pending confirmation before submitting the new message.
237:               Go back to Step 5.
238: 
239:         "RESPOND" →
240:           Read the recentMessages array. Handle every event:
241: 
242:           Event "message" (Pexo sent text):
243:             Relay Pexo's text to the user in full.
244:             If Pexo asked a question, wait for the user's answer.
245:             Then run: pexo-chat.sh <project_id> "{user's exact answer}"
246:             Go back to Step 5.
247: 
248:           Event "preview_video" (Pexo sent preview options):
249:             For each assetId in assetIds:
250:               Run: pexo-asset-get.sh <project_id> <assetId>
251:               Copy the "url" field from the returned JSON.
252:             Show all preview URLs to the user with labels (A, B, C...).
253:             Ask the user to pick one.
254:             After user picks:
255:               Run: pexo-chat.sh <project_id> "{user's choice}" --choice <selected_asset_id>
256:             Go back to Step 5.
257: 
258:           Event "document":
259:             Mention the document to the user.
260: 
261:           Event "attachment":
262:             Fetch each assetId with pexo-asset-get.sh and deliver the resulting file or URL.
263: 
264:         "DELIVER" →
265:           Go to Step 7.
266: 
267:         "FAILED" →
268:           Go to Step 8.
269: 
270:         "RECONNECT" →
271:           Run: pexo-chat.sh <project_id> "continue"
272:           Tell the user the connection was interrupted and you are reconnecting.
273:           Go back to Step 5.
274: 
275: Step 7. Deliver the final video.
276: 
277:         7a. Relay any message events in recentMessages, then find the final_video
278:             event and get its assetId.
279: 
280:         7b. Decide the download variant from the user's request:
281:             - Default: download without a watermark.
282:             - If the user explicitly asks to keep, show, or add a watermark, use
283:               the watermarked variant.
284:             - Both variants require an active subscription or watermark whitelist.
285: 
286:         7c. Run one of:
287:             - pexo-asset-get.sh <project_id> <assetId>
288:               (default, no watermark)
289:             - pexo-asset-get.sh <project_id> <assetId> --with-watermark
290:               (only when explicitly requested)
291: 
292:         7d. Show the downloaded video file to the user.
293: 
294:         7e. Also send the user a message (in their language) with:
295:             - The video download URL (copy the "url" field from the JSON output).
296:               Send the FULL URL as plain text, including all query parameters.
297:               Example:
298:               https://pexo-assets.oss-us-east-1.aliyuncs.com/projects%2F123%2Fassets%2Fvideo.mp4?OSSAccessKeyId=xxx&Expires=xxx&Signature=xxx
299:             - Project page: https://pexo.ai/project/{project_id}
300:             - Ask if satisfied or want revisions.
301: 
302:         Common delivery mistakes to avoid:
303:         ✗ Truncated URL (missing ?OSSAccessKeyId=...&Signature=...) → 403 Forbidden
304:         ✗ Markdown wrapped [text](url) → URL breaks on some platforms
305: 
306: Step 8. Handle failure.
307: 
308:         8a. Read failureReason, nextActionHint, and recentMessages from the JSON.
309:         8b. If failureReason is "INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS":
310:               Tell the user prominently that production stopped because the account
311:               has insufficient credits.
312:               Go to Credit Error Handling below. Do not offer or attempt a retry
313:               until the user confirms that credits have been added.
314:             Otherwise, if stderr from the failed command contains "Credits balance",
315:             "credits", or "Insufficient credits":
316:               Go to Credit Error Handling below.
317:             Otherwise, send the user a message (in their language) with:
318:               - What went wrong (explain nextActionHint in simple terms)
319:               - Project page: https://pexo.ai/project/{project_id}
320:               - Offer to retry.
321: 
322: Step 9. Timeout.
323: 
324:         If you have been in the Step 5 loop for more than 30 minutes
325:         and nextAction is still "WAIT":
326: 
327:         Send the user a message (in their language) with:
328:         - The video is taking longer than expected.
329:         - Project page: https://pexo.ai/project/{project_id}
330:         - Help guide: https://pexo.ai/connect/openclaw
331:         - Ask whether to keep waiting or start over.
332:         Stop polling. Wait for user instructions.
333: ```
334: 
335: ### Credit Error Handling
336: 
337: Use this flow when `pexo-project-get.sh` returns
338: `failureReason: "INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS"`, or when a command fails and stderr
339: contains credit-related information (look for: "Credits balance", "credits",
340: or "Insufficient credits"):
341: 
342: ```
343: Step A. If stderr contains a purchase link and instructions, send them
344:         to the user (in their language).
345: 
346: Step B. If stderr only contains the error message without a purchase link,
347:         send the user a message (in their language) with:
348:         - Their credits are insufficient.
349:         - To add credits: visit https://pexo.ai/home?billing=credits
350:           and complete the purchase flow.
351: 
352: Step C. After the user confirms they have added credits, retry the failed step.
353: ```
354: 
355: ### Revising an Existing Video
356: 
357: ```
358: Step 1. Use the same project_id.
359: Step 2. Run: pexo-chat.sh <project_id> "{user's exact feedback}"
360: Step 3. Go to Step 5 of the main workflow (start polling).
361: ```
362: 
363: ---
364: 
365: ## Asset Upload
366: 
367: Pexo can process a public `https://` webpage URL when it is included verbatim in the user's
368: brief. Pass that webpage URL to Pexo; do not scrape or download the page locally.
369: 
370: For a direct image, video, or audio file URL, ask for explicit approval before downloading it,
371: then upload the downloaded file. Only fetch public `https://` URLs. Never fetch `http://`,
372: localhost, loopback, link-local, private-network, credential-bearing, or signed/private URLs;
373: ask the user to upload those files directly instead.
374: 
375: Upload and reference workflow:
376: ```bash
377: # Upload the file
378: asset_id=$(pexo-upload.sh <project_id> photo.jpg)
379: 
380: # Reference the asset in your message to Pexo
381: pexo-chat.sh <project_id> "Here is the product photo <original-image>${asset_id}</original-image>, please use it as reference"
382: ```
383: 
384: Tag formats:
385: ```
386: <original-image>asset-id</original-image>
387: <original-video>asset-id</original-video>
388: <original-audio>asset-id</original-audio>
389: ```
390: 
391: Tags are mandatory. Bare asset IDs in pexo-chat.sh messages are ignored by Pexo.
392: 
393: ---
394: 
395: ## Important Rules
396: 
397: ### Polling
398: - During WAIT: only call pexo-project-get.sh. Calling pexo-chat.sh during WAIT triggers duplicate video production.
399: - Wait at least 60 seconds between each pexo-project-get.sh call.
400: - Process every event in recentMessages, not just the first one.
401: 
402: ### Credit Confirmation
403: - Treat `nextAction=CONFIRM` as a user decision point, not as WAIT or RESPOND.
404: - Only run `pexo-billing-confirm.sh` after the user explicitly approves the displayed estimate;
405:   pass `--user-approved` to record that prior approval. The script refuses to contact Pexo
406:   without this flag and emits a visible approval event.
407: - Use the `confirmation_id` returned by `pexo-project-get.sh`; confirmation IDs apply only to the current pending batch.
408: - A revised message sent with `pexo-chat.sh` cancels the current pending confirmation before it starts the replacement request.
409: 
410: ### Delivery
411: - Copy the "url" field from pexo-asset-get.sh output. Send it as plain text with all query parameters.
412: - Treat the script's `withWatermark` field as the authoritative selected variant.
413: - Do not claim a clean download if the request failed or `withWatermark` is not false.
414: - Show the downloaded video file to the user when possible.
415: 
416: ### Projects
417: - New video → pexo-project-create.sh to create a new project.
418: - Revisions → reuse the existing project_id.
419: 
420: ### Cost
421: - Each message to Pexo costs tokens. Consolidate information into one message when possible.
422: - For `nextAction=FAILED`, use `failureReason` for remediation. Do not infer a failure category from `nextActionHint` text.
423:

426: ## Script Reference
427: 
428: | Script | Usage | Returns |
429: |---|---|---|
430: | `pexo-project-create.sh` | `[project_name]` or `--name <n>` | `project_id` string. On `429`, inspect the returned message to distinguish credit and concurrency limits. |
431: | `pexo-project-list.sh` | `[page_size]` or `--page <n> --page-size <n>` | Projects JSON |
432: | `pexo-project-get.sh` | `<project_id> [--full-history]` | JSON with `nextAction`, `nextActionHint`, `recentMessages`; `CONFIRM` includes `confirmation`; recognized `FAILED` states include `failureReason`, and error events retain `errorCode`, `errorMessage`, and `toolCallId` |
433: | `pexo-upload.sh` | `<project_id> <file_path>` | `asset_id` string |

435: | `pexo-billing-confirm.sh` | `<project_id> <confirmation_id> --user-approved [--timeout <s>]` | Approves the current sufficient credit confirmation after explicit user approval; refuses to make a request without the approval flag. |
436: | `pexo-asset-get.sh` | `<project_id> <asset_id> [--with-watermark]` | JSON with video details, selected `url`, `localPath`, and `withWatermark` |
